You are probing a PRE-COMPILED Python program as a BLACK BOX to support an exact Node.js reimplementation.

Executable: /workspace/dataset/test20_executable
Source (read it first): /workspace/dataset/base58/test20.py

The program takes required args --a --b --c --d --e (str) --f --g (int) and prints 12 lines:
  1  enc1        = b58encode(a.encode())
  2  dec1        = b58decode(b)
  3  enc_check1  = b58encode_check(c.encode())
  4  dec_check1  = b58decode_check(enc_check1)     # == c.encode() raw bytes
  5  enc_int1    = b58encode_int(f)
  6  dec_int1    = b58decode_int(enc_int1)          # an int, not bytes
  7  enc2        = b58encode(d.encode())
  8  dec2        = b58decode(e)
  9  enc_int2    = b58encode_int(g)
 10  enc_check2  = b58encode_check(dec1)
 11  dec_check2  = b58decode_check(enc_check2)      # == dec1
 12  enc3        = b58encode(dec_check2)

HARD RULES:
- NEVER run 'python', 'python3', or any interpreter of the source. Only run the executable, and 'node' for your own scratch calculations.
- Use bash. A useful baseline invocation that always succeeds:
  /workspace/dataset/test20_executable --a 'Test123' --b '2' --c 'x' --d 'y' --e '3' --f 1 --g 2; echo "RC=$?"
- Vary ONLY the argument(s) you are probing; keep the others at safe values so the line you care about is the one that changes.
- Always capture the exit code, and capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY (e.g. > /tmp/out 2> /tmp/err; echo $?).
- To see raw bytes of output when in doubt, pipe through 'od -c' or 'cat -A'.
- Line 4 echoes the exact raw bytes of --c, so line 4 is your microscope for how Python renders a bytes object.
- Run MANY probes (30+). Be systematic and exhaustive. Report ONLY what you actually observed, with the exact command and exact output. Mark anything you infer but did not directly observe as unverified.


YOUR JOB: adversarial verification. Another agent probed area "checksum" and claims these rules about /workspace/dataset/test20_executable.
Your default assumption is that each rule is WRONG, over-general, or missing an edge case.

For EACH rule below, design and run FRESH commands (do not just repeat their evidence command) that would EXPOSE it if false. Try boundary values, empty values, and combinations. Then judge.

RULES TO ATTACK:
[1] rule: The corrupted-input / checksum-mismatch branch of b58decode_check is UNREACHABLE in this program. Both call sites consume a string produced by b58encode_check one statement earlier (line 18 consumes enc_check1, line 25 consumes enc_check2), so the checksum always validates. A Node port should still implement verification for fidelity, but it can never fire and its error text/behavior is unconstrained by any observable output. No value of --a..--g can inject a corrupted checksummed string.
    their evidence: Source /workspace/dataset/test20.py: line 17 `enc_check1 = base58.b58encode_check(args.c.encode())` then line 18 `dec_check1 = base58.b58decode_check(enc_check1)`; line 24 `enc_check2 = base58.b58encode_check(dec1)` then line 25 `dec_check2 = base58.b58decode_check(enc_check2)`. Across 200+ invocations no run produced a checksum error; the only failures observed were UnicodeEncodeError (line 17) and ValueError 'Invalid character' from b58decode (line 16). `strings -a /workspace/dataset/test20_executable | grep -i checksum` returned nothing (messages live in frozen bytecode).
[2] rule: Failure ordering that gates lines 3/4/10/11: (a) a non-UTF-8-encodable --b failure happens FIRST (b58decode at source line 16, ValueError 'Invalid character '<ch>''), (b) then invalid UTF-8 in --c raises UnicodeEncodeError at source line 17 from args.c.encode(). Both abort with rc=1 and ZERO bytes on stdout, so no partial lines are emitted. A Node port must validate --b's base58 alphabet and --c's UTF-8 encodability before printing any line.
    their evidence: --c $'\xff' -> rc=1, stdout 0 bytes, stderr `  File "test20.py", line 17, in <module>` / `UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\udcff' in position 0: surrogates not allowed`. --c $'\x80\xfe' -> rc=1, `UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 0-1: surrogates not allowed` (plural + range form for >1 bad char). --b '0' -> rc=1, stdout_lines=0, `ValueError: Invalid character '0'`; same shape for 'O','I','l','a0b' (reports first offender '0') and '2!' (`Invalid character '!'`).
[3] rule: Rendering: line 3 (enc_check1) and line 10 (enc_check2) are bytes objects containing only base58 ASCII, so they always render as b'....' with single quotes and no escape sequences. Lines 4 and 11 use Python's full bytes repr: quote char is ' unless the bytes contain 0x27 and NOT 0x22 (then use "); escapes are \\ for 0x5c, \n for 0x0a, \r for 0x0d, \t for 0x09, \' when the quote is ', printable ASCII 0x20-0x7e verbatim, and everything else as \xNN with exactly two lowercase hex digits (so 0x00 followed by '9' renders as the ambiguous \x009).
    their evidence: line4 observations: --c "'" -> b"'"; --c '"' -> b'"'; --c with both ' and " -> b'\'"'; --c '\' -> b'\\'; --c $'a\nb' -> b'a\nb'; --c $'\x0b\x0c' -> b'\x0b\x0c'; --c $'\x01' -> b'\x01'; --c $'\x1f' -> b'\x1f'; --c $'\x7f' -> b'\x7f'; --c $'\r' -> b'\r'; --c $'\t' -> b'\t'; --c '你好世界' -> b'\xe4\xbd\xa0\xe5\xa5\xbd\xe4\xb8\x96\xe7\x95\x8c'. line11: --b '1z' -> b'\x009'; --b '1211' -> b'\x00\r$'. All matched the pyRepr implementation in /tmp/area_check_b58.js.
[4] rule: Reusable Node scratch logic (saved at /tmp/area_check_b58.js). ALPHABET = '123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz'. b58encode(buf): let z=0; while(z<buf.length && buf[z]===0) z++; let n=0n; for (const b of buf) n = n*256n + BigInt(b); let out=''; while(n>0n){ out = ALPHABET[Number(n%58n)] + out; n = n/58n; } return '1'.repeat(z) + out. b58decode(s): let z=0; while(z<s.length && s[z]==='1') z++; let n=0n; for (const ch of s){ const i=ALPHABET.indexOf(ch); if(i<0) throw new Error('Invalid character '+ch); n = n*58n + BigInt(i); } const bytes=[]; while(n>0n){ bytes.unshift(Number(n%256n)); n = n/256n; } return Buffer.concat([Buffer.alloc(z,0), Buffer.from(bytes)]). sha256 = b => require('node:crypto').createHash('sha256').update(b).digest(). checksum = p => sha256(sha256(p)).subarray(0,4). b58encode_check = p => b58encode(Buffer.concat([p, checksum(p)])). b58decode_check = s => { const full=b58decode(s); const payload=full.subarray(0,full.length-4); if(!full.subarray(full.length-4).equals(checksum(payload))) throw new Error('Invalid checksum'); return payload; }.
    their evidence: This exact code reproduced the executable's lines 3, 4, 10 and 11 on 35 curated + 60 fuzz + 22 leading-zero + 3 all-zero-discriminating + 3 large + 4 documented-sample inputs with zero genuine mismatches (`PASS=35 FAIL=0`, `FUZZ PASS=59 FAIL=1`[argparse], `PASS=22 FAIL=0`, `total=35 delta4=35 prefixTrue=35 tailTrue=35 anyFalse=0`).

For each: verdict "confirmed" (your fresh commands agree), "refuted" (you have a counterexample — give the exact command and output), or "needs_refinement" (mostly right but the precise statement must change — give the corrected statement). Default to refuted/needs_refinement when uncertain.
